sources.citation: Dakubu, Mary Esther Kropp. 2016. Review of Dombrowsky-Hahn 2015, A grammar of Syer. Journal of African Languages and Linguistics 37(2): 287-294. doi:10.1515/jall-2016-0012 (open copy served by the book's publisher, Köppe).
sources.note: pp. 287-288: the grammar's Phonology chapter 'is thus essentially about segmental phonology, with little attention to suprasegmentals and prosody except for a tantalizingly brief and undeveloped reference to syllable stress (16). Stress (also referred to as accent) appears to be relevant to intervocalic consonant weakening (22, 26), and is a conditioning factor in the palatalization of consonants (40, 41).... specific comment on its realization would have been welcome.' Also: 'Syer has three phonemic tones... a tone tune is a property of a word' (p. 288, citing the grammar p. 114). The review…

sources.citation: Prost, André. 1964. Tenyer. In Contribution à l'étude des langues voltaïques (Mémoires de l'IFAN 70), 213-247. Dakar: IFAN. Chapitre I 'La phonétique du tenyer', pp. 215-216 (Rosetta Project scan of the phonology pages only).
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: library print copy (Scan & Deliver or loan); the journal or volume is held, not the item itself: TOZ Offsite Storage L.SOC.42.105.28.7.65 (70)
sources.note: Silent on stress/accent. The phonology sketch covers vowels, semi-vowels, consonants and '4. Les tons' only: 'Notre enquête a été beaucoup trop rapide pour nous permettre l'étude tonétique de la langue. Il appert néanmoins que dans la 3e classe, les mots terminés en l forment leur pluriel par un tonème... Nous ne donnons que le ton « relatif »' (p. 216). No word 'accent' anywhere in the scanned pages.

sources.citation: Wichser, Madlen & Marlis Bühler. 1979. Description phonologique du karaboro. Ouagadougou: Société Internationale de Linguistique. (Rosetta Project scan of selected pages.) SIBLING LANGUAGE ONLY: Eastern Karaboro / Kar [xrb], glottocode east2398.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: HathiTrust digitized, search-only (in copyright); interlibrary loan
sources.note: Not the target language. Its 'traits prosodiques' (§5.3) are nasalisation, longueur, glottalisation, vélarisation and tone; the scanned text contains no 'accent'/'intensité' mention. Recorded only to show that the nearest SIL phonology of Karaboro is also silent on stress.

sources.citation: Prost, André. 1964. Tenyer (introductory page 'Les Karaboro' and glossed-text pages), same volume.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Identifies the variety: 'les Tenyem parlant le tenyer à Tengrela, les Syem parlant le syer à Banfora, les Kleb parlant le kler à l'est de Banfora; le dialecte étudié ici est le tenyer'.

sources.citation: Dombrowsky-Hahn, Klaudia. 2015. A grammar of Syer (Western Karaboro, Senufo): phonology, morphology, argument realization. (Gur Monographs 12.) Köln: Rüdiger Köppe. XX+582 pp. ISBN 978-3-89645-612-0.

sources.note: The only full modern description; per Dakubu's review it contains a brief reference to syllable stress on p. 16 and invokes stress/accent as a conditioning factor for intervocalic weakening (pp. 22, 26) and palatalization (pp. 40-41). Pages 15-17 (2.1 Syllable structure) and 40-41 would settle whether any placement statement exists. TOC shows no stress heading.
